transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hey, Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. Um, well, I guess what made me come in is that for the past year or so, the smallest thing just pulls me off what I’m doing before I can stop it. I mean, it could be a phone buzz, or somebody walking past my office, or... or even just a random thought about my in-laws. 

Which, honestly, my father-in-law just bought this massive RV, right? Drove it all the way down here last week and parked it right in my driveway. I told my wife our HOA is gonna throw an absolute fit because it's blocking the sidewalk, but he refuses to sleep in our guest room. We just bought a brand new mattress for that room, too. Top of the line, memory foam, but he says it sleeps too hot. I don't know how a mattress sleeps hot, but whatever, it's his back. 

Um... wait, sorry, what was I saying? Right, why I'm here. Yeah, just... every little thought or noise like that just completely derails me before I can catch myself.
Looking back at your childhood, did you struggle with this same type of distractibility or difficulty staying on task in school?

Oh, yeah, for sure. Looking back, this was definitely around when I was a kid, too. My teachers were always moving my seat because I talked way too much, or I'd just get up without asking, or I'd blurt things out before they even finished the question. 

I remember Mrs. Gable in 7th grade actually put my desk right next to her filing cabinet, facing the blank wall. Which is ironic, you know, because I didn't even finish high school, but now I'm the CEO of my own company and I have this massive corner office. Floor-to-ceiling windows. Though honestly, those windows are a huge pain to keep clean. We hired this new commercial cleaning crew last month, and they use this awful lemon-scented spray that gives my assistant a migraine. She's been complaining about it non-stop, so I had to call building management yesterday to tell them to switch back to the blue stuff. The blue stuff leaves streaks when the afternoon sun hits it, but at least nobody's getting sick, right? 

Um... but yeah, school. Sorry. Yeah, I've pretty much always been like that. Just couldn't stay in my seat or keep quiet.
